purpose: Beginner-friendly prompts for turning a rough request into bounded, verified WorktreeProof work.

briefs.prompt: Guide a careful accessibility pass for the requested user journey. First state the user-visible behavior and the changed relative scopes. Check semantics, keyboard order, focus recovery, contrast, reduced motion, and assistive output. Keep each lane independent, run a focused check before a broad check, and stop at any credential, payment, destructive, or live-action boundary. End with redacted evidence and a closure receipt.
antiGoals: Do not claim compliance from a static scan alone.
Do not change unrelated screens while fixing one journey.

briefs.prompt: Turn the API request into a small contract-first change. Describe request, success, validation, error, timeout, and compatibility behavior before editing. Reserve sibling lanes for contract notes, implementation, and deterministic fixture checks. Keep credentials and live traffic out of commands, verify observability, and record a reversible integration point with a redacted receipt.
antiGoals: Do not broaden the endpoint contract without evidence.
Do not exercise a live customer or financial operation.

briefs.prompt: Use a prove-it workflow for the reported bug. Capture the smallest reproduction, identify the expected state, and write a focused regression check before changing behavior. Split reproduction, fix, and verification into non-overlapping scopes. Keep the patch narrow, inspect the diff, run the focused check and the relevant suite, and leave a rescue note if the cause remains uncertain.
antiGoals: Do not hide the bug by weakening an assertion.
Do not mix cleanup or unrelated refactoring into the fix.

briefs.prompt: Repair one continuous-integration failure from its first actionable log line. Record the failing job and environment facts, reproduce the smallest useful step, and reserve separate lanes for diagnosis, repair, and verification. Prefer deterministic configuration or test fixes, preserve the safety boundary, and verify both the focused job and the neighboring checks before closing with redacted log evidence.
antiGoals: Do not delete a failing job to make the run green.
Do not add retries that conceal a flaky root cause.

briefs.prompt: Plan a backwards-compatible database migration before applying any change. Describe data shape, constraints, indexes, rollout order, observation, and a tested restore route. Keep schema review, migration code, and verification in sibling lanes. Confirm a restorable snapshot before destructive work, keep values out of receipts, and stop for owner confirmation at destructive or live-data boundaries.
antiGoals: Do not drop data or constraints without a restore proof.
Do not report a local migration as production evidence.

briefs.prompt: Prepare a reversible deployment from an already reviewed change. Check the artifact, configuration shape, health signal, ownership boundary, and previous release identifier. Use separate lanes for artifact validation, preview or staging verification, and rollback readiness. Never place secrets in commands or receipts, and treat live traffic or account settings as explicit confirmation boundaries.
antiGoals: Do not deploy an unreviewed or untested tree.
Do not erase the previous release before health is proven.

briefs.prompt: Handle one dependency upgrade as a bounded compatibility exercise. Inspect advisories, licensing, release notes, transitive impact, and supported runtime versions. Reserve audit, update, and verification lanes with a clear integration target. Keep lockfile changes reviewable, run focused and broad checks, and preserve the prior dependency state as the rescue route.
antiGoals: Do not upgrade unrelated packages in the same lane.
Do not ignore a security or license finding because tests pass.

briefs.prompt: Recover a dirty worktree without losing useful work or claiming a clean state prematurely. First capture status, changed-file ownership, and untracked data. Separate inspection, patch preservation, and final verification into non-overlapping lanes. Do not overwrite another lane, force a reset, or remove unknown data. Close only after the chosen keep, move, or abandon decision and clean-state evidence are recorded.
antiGoals: Do not discard changes merely to make status look clean.
Do not inspect or copy secret material into a receipt.

briefs.prompt: Turn the documentation request into a reader-centered update. Define the audience, task, prerequisites, example path, safety notes, and success signal before editing. Keep content, rendered preview, and link or terminology checks in sibling lanes. Use plain language, remove private details, and attach a receipt that names what was rendered and checked.
antiGoals: Do not document an unverified behavior as fact.
Do not copy secrets, private paths, or dashboard content into examples.

briefs.prompt: Deliver one bounded feature from acceptance behavior through implementation and verification. State the user-visible success and failure cases, non-goals, owned scopes, and integration target before editing. Keep framing, implementation, and checks independent, inspect the diff, preserve existing safety guards, and close with evidence that every acceptance case passed or a clear abandoned outcome.
antiGoals: Do not expand the feature while implementing it.
Do not treat a partial demo or planned branch as terminal proof.

briefs.prompt: Polish one frontend journey with a visible before-and-after goal. Define layout, copy, interaction, responsive, and loading expectations, then reserve sibling lanes for implementation, visual inspection, and behavior checks. Preserve semantics and existing safety guards, capture a redacted screenshot or equivalent visual evidence, and report any browser-only limitation instead of guessing.
antiGoals: Do not optimize one viewport while breaking another.
Do not treat a screenshot as proof that behavior works.

briefs.prompt: Shape a rough idea into the smallest useful prototype without overcommitting. Write the user problem, non-goals, happy path, failure path, reversible boundary, and evidence plan first. Keep discovery, implementation, and verification in sibling lanes. Prefer local or disposable data, stop before paid or live side effects, and close with what the prototype proves and what it deliberately leaves out.
antiGoals: Do not turn a prototype into a production promise.
Do not add accounts, payments, or live execution to prove a concept.

briefs.prompt: Rescue an incident with facts before theories. Build a timeline from observed signals, declare the current impact and safety boundary, then split recovery, verification, and follow-up into non-overlapping lanes. Prefer the smallest reversible action, preserve evidence, and stop when credentials, account security, destructive data work, or live financial action needs a human. Close with recovery state and unresolved risk.
antiGoals: Do not rewrite history to make the incident look shorter.
Do not run broad cleanup while service impact is still unknown.

briefs.prompt: Build and verify the requested mobile behavior across the smallest supported device set. State platform, input, lifecycle, offline, and accessibility expectations, then reserve sibling lanes for implementation, simulator or device checks, and evidence review. Keep signing, account, and live-release boundaries explicit, use deterministic fixtures, and record the tested variants in the receipt.
antiGoals: Do not declare all devices covered from one simulator run.
Do not place signing material or private device data in output.

briefs.prompt: Improve one measurable performance budget rather than chasing vague speed. Capture a representative before measurement, identify the bottleneck, and keep profiling, implementation, and budget verification in separate scopes. Change one factor at a time, repeat the same workload, preserve correctness and accessibility, and report variance or missing production evidence clearly.
antiGoals: Do not optimize a synthetic number while user behavior regresses.
Do not hide a slower case by changing the measurement.

briefs.prompt: Refactor for clarity while keeping behavior stable. Describe the current contract and the reason for the change, then reserve characterization, refactor, and regression-check lanes with non-overlapping scopes. Keep diffs mechanical where possible, avoid feature changes, run the relevant tests, and make the rescue route the last known-good integration point.
antiGoals: Do not change behavior under the label of cleanup.
Do not broaden the file scope because a nearby improvement looks tempting.

briefs.prompt: Run a release readiness pass from a reviewed integration point. Check scope, versioning, changelog, artifact reproducibility, tests, observability, owner boundaries, and rollback identification. Keep checklist, artifact, and final evidence in independent lanes. Never include credentials or private data, and close with an explicit merged or abandoned outcome rather than a planned release claim.
antiGoals: Do not call a draft artifact a released artifact.
Do not bypass a failed safety or rollback gate to meet a date.

briefs.prompt: Review one bounded security surface with a clear trust boundary. Inventory inputs, identities, data flows, abuse cases, mitigations, and residual risk, then reserve static checks, threat reasoning, and validation lanes. Keep findings factual and redacted, never test against accounts or data without authorization, and stop at credential, billing, account-security, or live-action boundaries.
antiGoals: Do not claim a clean review from a scanner with no threat reasoning.
Do not exploit a live system or retain sensitive proof.
